neighbours.label: Employment context where 'fire' / 'dismiss' is the expected next word: the token just before a verb of firing an employee ("disciplining or …", "Can my boss …", "appoints and may …")
fire: It is illegal for a company to demote or fire a worker for joining a union.
Can my manager fire me because I refused to work on Sunday?
The mayor hires and may dismiss the police chief at any time.
The owner threatened to suspend or fire anyone who spoke to the press.
After the audit, the directors voted to dismiss the finance officer.
Under the contract, the school cannot discipline or dismiss a teacher without a hearing.
Is my employer allowed to fire me while I am on maternity leave?
The coach lost eleven games in a row, and the club decided to sack him.
quiet: It is illegal for a company to dump or burn waste near the river.
Can my manager see the files that I saved on the shared drive?
The mayor opens and may address the council meeting at any time.
The owner promised to repaint or replace any fence damaged by the storm.
After the audit, the directors voted to publish the annual accounts.
Under the contract, the school cannot sell or lease the playing field without a vote.
Is my employer allowed to move my desk while I am on holiday?
The coach won eleven games in a row, and the club decided to extend his contract.
